title: Cross-region replay: reconcile tokenizer drift and billing mismatches for locale-variant clients
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Symptoms: Several invoices (internal pilot customers and a customer in EU) include apparent overcharges or missing credits for replayed requests originating from different regions. Root cause hypothesis: cross-region replays pass through different tokenizer versions or locale-sensitive unicode normalizers (e.g., ICU settings), resulting in divergent token counts between the serving region and the billing reconciliation job. This manifests when a request is served in region A, then replayed / reprocessed in region B for retry/async postprocessing (e.g., offline rerank, replay audit, or fixup). The metering pipeline currently relies on the token_count reported by the serving runtime plus a per-request tokenizer fingerprint that is optional. If the fingerprint is absent or inconsistent, downstream accounting normalizes token counts with the local tokenizer, producing mismatch and billing drift.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate a short prompt containing locale-specific sequences (e.g., emoji+zwj sequences, combining marks, CJK halfwidth/fullwidth variants, and German ß vs 'ss' normalization) from a client set to locale 'de-DE' routed to region EU-1.
2) Serve the request in EU-1 using tokenizer v2.1 (current runtime). Log reported token_count=37 and include tokenizer_hash in metadata.

3) Force an async replay that is routed to us-west-2 (US) where the reconciliation job uses tokenizer v2.0 and default unicode normalization. Replayed job recalculates token_count=42 and writes an accounting row.
4) Observe mismatch on billing ledger: original_charge != reconciled_charge, triggers alert from the billing anomaly detector.
observed_behavior: Divergent token counts recorded by serving region and reconciliation/backfill region for the same logical request. Leads to either ghost charges (double-billing) or missing credits depending on aggregation order. Alert noise increased by ~3x for customer pilot clusters in Feb, with two customers reporting unexpected invoice deltas ~4-9% on heavy multilingual workloads.
expected_behavior: Tokenization and normalization must be canonical and reproducible across regions and replayed workflows. Metering pipeline should either accept authoritative token_count from the serving runtime with strong provenance or deterministically recompute counts using an explicit, versioned tokenizer and normalization config embedded in the request metadata.
hypothesis_and_root_causes: Tokenization/version skew: different runtime tokenizer binaries or models between regions (v2.0 vs v2.1).
Missing/optional tokenizer fingerprint: some proxies/SDKs omit tokenizer_hash, making downstream recompute non-deterministic.
Locale-driven unicode normalization: different ICU/normalization settings at region boundaries leading to different codepoint sequences after normalization, affecting token splits.
Compression/path transformations: proxies that decode/encode compressed payloads may inadvertently alter byte-level representation of combining marks.
Asymmetric replay routing: replay jobs land in region with different runtime that lacks backward-compatible tokenizer mapping table.
proposed_solutions: A) Enforce authoritative token_count propagation: require runtime to emit token_count and tokenizer_hash; downstream billing jobs must prefer authoritative count when hash present. (Fast path, low-infra change, needs audit)

B) Canonical tokenizer re-evaluation: bundle tokenizer artifacts (or fingerprint-to-binary mapping) in a hashed manifest; reconciliation workers must rehydrate the original tokenizer using the fingerprint to recompute deterministically. (Stronger correctness, larger infra/size impact)

C) Normalization canonicalization: standardize and document exact Unicode normalization form (NFC/NFD) and ICU version across regions; add middleware in ingress to canonicalize bytes before tokenization.

D) Backfill reconciliation tool: a correction pipeline that identifies mismatch rows where authoritative fingerprint disagree and generates retroactive ledger adjustments with audit trail and customer notification hooks.
E) Telemetry + detection: add metric 'metering.tokenizer_hash_missing' and build a daily drift report to signal regions with high skew.
proposed_acceptance_criteria: 1) A production test (small canary) demonstrates that replayed requests with tokenizer_hash produce identical token_count across eu-1 and us-west-2 when using solution A or B.
2) Billing reconciliation job accepts authoritative token_count when tokenizer_hash present; no new mismatches observed for canary workload for 72h.
3) Rolling rollout plan documented and signoffs from Runtime, Billing, and Compliance.
4) Telemetry added and dashboard in Console showing tokenizer_hash coverage by region and SDK versions.
implementation_notes: Initial POC: implement authoritative-count preference in the reconciliation worker as a feature flag. Add request metadata validation in the runtime to always emit tokenizer_hash and token_count. Register mapping of tokenizer_hash -> tokenizer_spec URI in internal artifact store. Work with infra to allow reconciliation workers to pull tokenizer artifacts (readonly) for deterministically recomputing counts (if needed). Expect cross-team coordination: Runtime (to change emitted metadata), Billing (reconciler changes), Infra (artifact hosting), QA (multilingual test corpus), DevExp/SDK (ensure SDKs propagate metadata).
risk_and_tradeoffs: Favoring authoritative token_count (A) is fastest but requires trust: if runtime incorrectly reports token_count (bug/attack), downstream cannot detect without fingerprint. Solution B is safer but heavier. Canonical normalization (C) reduces future surface but may break clients relying on different normalization. Backfill adjustments (D) have customer communication risk. We'll stagger features behind flags and limit initial rollouts to pilot customers.
testing_plan: 1) Create deterministic multilingual test vectors (50 prompts) with expected token counts under each tokenizer version. 2) Unit tests for reconciliation preferring authoritative token_count. 3) Integration test that starts a request in eu-1, replays in us-west-2 with and without tokenizer_hash to assert counts. 4) Fuzz harness to detect edge sequences (ZWJ, combining marks, mixed directionality).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary, 1 week): enable runtime metadata emission and reconciliation worker flag for one pilot customer and internal traffic. Phase 2 (Gradual, 3 weeks): expand to all EU and one NA region. Phase 3 (Global): enable authoritative-count by default and deprecate recompute path after 90 days of stable telemetry.
notes_for_reviewers: Reviewers: focus on compatibility implications of authoritative-count. Check that fallback recompute path is still available for forensic re-evaluation and that artifact hosting has correct access controls. Security: tokenization artifacts must not contain sensitive customer data and should be served from read-only artifact store.
